newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish share jump 8.02 pct in heavy volume.
newsitem.headline: Turkish share jump 8.02 pct in heavy volume.

text.p: Istanbul shares recouped a considerable part of the recent sharp losses by surging an average 8.02 percent in strong volume on Thursday as political tension eased, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed up 110 points at 1,482, but down from a day's high of 1,502. It had dived 14.9 percent in the past three days. Trade volume surged to 38.96 trillion lira ($313.4 million) from Wednesday's 15.20 trillion ($122.5 million).
Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan signed on late Wednesday a key National Security Council (MGK) document.

Political uncertainty had mounted earlier in the week due to a row between the coalition's Islamist wing and the secularist military which had warned the government at last Friday's MGK meeting to rein in what it saw as rising Islamist zeal.

"All markets reacted positively to Erbakan's signing of the MGK document. Share prices had become very low, so the news prompted heavy buying, particulary in companies with good 1996 profits" said Gursel Yildiz from Vakifbank.
Brokers see firm resistance at the index's 1,500 level, saying further progress in Erbakan's reconciliation move with the army and improvements in the ailing economy were needed for an upward trend.
